state.case_summary:
A 74-year-old Caucasian woman with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (diagnosed in 2006, complex karyotype with TP53 mutation and trisomy 12) was receiving zanubrutinib and subcutaneous immunoglobulin replacement for hypogammaglobulinemia. In May 2022 she was hospitalized for pulmonary sepsis, treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics and caspofungin, with resolution. One month later, she developed grade 4 neutropenia (<500/μL) for over 15 days and a febrile peak. Starting 15 June, tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions appeared on the lower limbs and then the upper limbs; the lesions progressed to central ulceration with a necrotic core. 

On 25 June, zanubrutinib was discontinued and oral itraconazole was begun after a 5 mm punch biopsy of a left-thigh lesion. Histopathological examination (HE, Giemsa, GMS, PAS, and Gram stains) showed severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation with minimal necrosis, angioinvasive microbial structures, thrombosed small vessels, and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells. Within vessels, thin-walled (5–15 μm), pauciseptate hyphae with minimal branching were seen, along with numerous thick-walled ovoid sporangia (5–20 μm) that stained strongly with PAS, GMS, and Giemsa. Only a presumptive diagnosis of deep cutaneous fungal infection was made at this time.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. mucormycosis
B. Parasitic infection
C. Invasive aspergillosis
D. Coccidioidomycosis (rhinococcidioidomycosis)
E. Chromoblastomycosis and scytalidosis
F. None
G. None
H. None

supporting_facts: complex karyotype with TP53 mutation and trisomy 12
tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions

excluded_candidates: Bacterial sepsis: although the patient had a history of pulmonary sepsis, the histopathological examination suggests a fungal infection
Viral infection: the presence of angioinvasive microbial structures and hyphal mats suggests a fungal infection rather than a viral one
salient_findings: cutaneous lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core
histopathological evidence of angioinvasive microbial structures
